all.reason: Recalibrate objectAllocation RAM on Neoverse-N2 from four complete five-round runs: this pull request's run 37950022133 (run median 0.298x) and three master controls, 37927504399 at d65703afaa (0.378x), 37902400038 at 438399d5f1 (0.380x) and 37889241211 at 8e6f2cf05 (0.363x). ParparVM's peak is bimodal on this runner, about 156-167 MB or about 123-129 MB against a steady 430 MB for JDK 25: the low mode is one round of fifteen on master (37889241211 round 5, 125.1 MB, 0.291x) and three rounds of five here (124.0, 128.6, 123.3 MB), so this run's median landed in it and failed as IMPROVED against a two-run 0.378x row that carried only the global 15% RAM tolerance. Whether this pull request makes the low mode more frequent (it adds -ffp-contract=off to the benchmark's native build and changes arraycopy/clone sizing for arrays of primitive arrays) or one run of five rounds simply drew it was NOT established: there is a single run of this branch. So this records no improvement. It keeps the baseline at the pooled run median (0.370x) and widens the RAM tolerance to the 30% the tool derives from the observed spread, which is what the objectAllocation rows of the other runners already carry; taking this run alone would have set 0.298x at 15% and failed the next high-mode run as a regression. Time is unchanged.

Recalibrate translator time and RAM on Xeon Platinum 8573C from three complete five-round runs. Run medians, time / RAM: this pull request's run 37974545389 at bb185e0f13, 0.638x / 0.430x; master 37927504399 at d65703afaa, the commit this branch is based on, 0.664x / 0.414x; master 37889241211 at 8e6f2cf05d, 0.521x / 0.465x. Master at the base commit fails the 0.505x / 0.517x row (which came from a single run) the same way this pull request does: time +31.5% there and +26.2% here against a 20% tolerance, RAM -19.9% there and -16.8% here against 15%. This pull request's medians lie between the two master runs on both metrics, and the two master runs differ from each other by more than this pull request differs from either. The shift is therefore present on master at the base commit and is not attributed to this pull request; why two runs of master differ this much was not investigated. No improvement or regression is claimed. The baseline moves to the pooled run medians and the time tolerance widens to the 30% the tool derives from the observed spread; RAM keeps the global tolerance.

The baseline moves to the pooled run median with the tolerance the tool derives. Time is unchanged.

Recalibrate translator time on AMD64 Family 25 Model 17 from five complete five-round runs. Run medians: this pull request's runs 38052037363 at bbeda29aaa (0.588x, which failed as IMPROVED at -24.4% against the 0.777x row's 20% tolerance), 38020026095 at f0abf10218 (0.756x, passed) and 37974545096 at bb185e0f13 (0.697x, passed), and two master controls, 38016546068 at 6dd059d34b (0.663x) and 37906860757 at 438399d5f1 (0.725x). The 0.777x row came from a single run and all five runs sit below it. Per round, master on this model ranges 0.545-0.749x and the failing run 0.527-0.788x, so master's own rounds reach the failing run's median. Master 438399d5f1 predates d65703afaa, the commit this branch is based on, and 6dd059d34b follows it. In the round timings the ratio moves with the JDK 25 arm rather than with ParparVM: in four of the runs JDK 25 took either 2.95-3.44 s or 4.31-5.20 s for the same workload while ParparVM took 2.27-2.94 s (2.33-2.77 s in the failing run, 2.27-2.94 s in master 38016546068). The failing run drew the slow JDK rounds in four of five, master 38016546068 in two of five, and this pull request's other two runs in one and two of five. The fifth run, master 37906860757, was slower in both arms (JDK 25 3.86-4.13 s with one round at 5.63 s, ParparVM 2.88-3.39 s). That is one run of this branch landing low while two others did not, so no improvement by this pull request is claimed; why the JDK arm has two speeds on this runner was not investigated, and two master runs cannot rule out a small shift inside this spread. The baseline moves to the pooled run median (0.697x) and the time tolerance widens to the 25% the tool derives from the observed spread. RAM is unchanged.
